policy: Every source IPA remains readable; changes are re-encodings, context allophones, or pronunciation variants rather than deletions.

changes: Independent Uxrowoiye glyph lineages retained
Vowel-final Polynesian phonotactics spreads
Consonant clusters coexist with vowel-dominant roots
Regularize contact repairs while maintaining older spellings
Separate W, F, V, Q and KS families begin merging into larger phonetic letter groups
Consonant-contact transitional vowels become more predictable
SOV starts to yield to SVO under particle licensing
Glottal and click remain recognizable as independent historical keys
Exactly 20 independent base letters established
B becomes the written host for B, F, V and W readings, selected by an accent
A no longer has a plain default pronunciation; every A phoneme has a quality accent
Clicks and glottal stops cease to be standard independent letters and become subscripts
Glottal pre-host; click post-host
Glottal lineage produces emphasis descendants > and <
Other major sound-family contrasts increasingly use accent selectors
Host letter plus two subscripts plus one accent per letter permitted
Standardize which subscripts are pre, below and post host
Stabilize two-subscript limit and historical pronunciation dictionary
Normalize accent selectors for vowels and consonant families
Allow syllabic and long-consonant metadata without extra glyph count
Default spoken syllables V, VV, CV, CVV
Preferred SVO remains while VSO becomes productive in marked constructions
Automatic epenthesis repairs new adjacent consonant pairs without rewriting inherited place names
Modern 20-letter base and stacked subscript writing applied consistently
Preserve historic proper name pronunciations alongside hypothetical modern readings
